areas.description: Twin entrances lead into the first chamber, where five hobgoblins are bunked on guard duty. At A is a wide underground stream used as a moat. Wooden planks about 15' long, used to cross it, are stored on the opposite side. A loud ox horn hangs on a peg and can be blown to attract someone to come put planks across; the hobgoblins in room 17 are tasked with this job. If intruders spend too long debating or making elaborate crossing plans, two hobgoblins from room 17 may appear. In the northwest corner at C is a crude hide painted to resemble stone, used for ambushes by hiding behind it and rushing out once intruders enter.
features: Wide underground stream used as a moat
Wooden planks about 15' long stored on the far side for crossing
Loud ox horn on a peg to summon hobgoblins from room 17 to lay the planks
Crude stone-painted hide in the northwest corner used for ambushes

areas.description: A 20' high hallway supported by three sets of pillars. The hobgoblins have rigged thin wires along the floor between the center two pillars.
areas.trap: Thin floor wires trigger a heavy stone-headed mallet swinging down from behind the pillars; it attacks as a 2 HD creature and deals 1d8 damage on a hit. A moment later a net covered in bells drops across the hall between the two pillars. Anyone caught is tangled for 1d6 rounds, and struggling causes the bells to ring loudly, likely alerting hobgoblins from room 17.
features: Three sets of pillars
20' high ceiling
Bell-covered net spanning the hall between the center pillars

areas.description: Six hobgoblins bunk here. They are not wearing armor but will don it if given time. The room has been fixed up, and what were once going to be platforms for caskets are now used as benches and tables. Three fancy elaborate red funeral shrouds with thin gold threading and black details are being used as hammocks.

encounters.count_note: AC 14 armored, 11 unarmored; movement 30' armored or 40' unarmored

treasure: Three funeral shrouds used as hammocks, worth 50 gp each
features: Former casket platforms repurposed as benches and tables
Three elaborate red funeral-shroud hammocks with thin gold threading and black details

areas.description: Usually this room is locked, though not very well. A thief could pick either door with ease, and the doors can be knocked in easily. The chief in room 21 has the key. It is full of odds and ends and minor plunder: clothing, sacks of grains and potatoes, hanging dried meats, perhaps some hanging 'fresh meat' in the form of slain foes, and mining tools such as picks, chisels, and hammers.
features: Stored clothing
Sacks of grain and potatoes
Hanging dried meats
Possibly hanging slain foes used as 'fresh meat'
Mining tools including picks, chisels, and hammers

areas.description: This room has been taken over by a skilled and tough hobgoblin who lives in luxury. On the wall are a short bow and two quivers of arrows, along with other items. He carries the key to this room on a string made of hair on his belt.

encounters.count_note: sub-leader; HD 3; armed with scimitar or short bow

features: Short bow on the wall
Two quivers of arrows on the wall
Luxurious living arrangements

areas.description: The hobgoblins here have piled up rubble in the hallway and stockpiled holy water to fend off the ghouls to the west.
features: Rubble piled up in the hallway as a defensive barrier

areas.description: This chamber contains the hobgoblin chief and three bodyguards. The chief has the key to the store room at 18. There is a plain bed, chairs, tables, and other furnishings here.

encounters.count_note: bodyguards; morale 9 while chief is present

treasure: Potion of Stone to Flesh (1 use)
Bag tied to the foot of the bed containing 600 gp, 1,200 sp, and 1,800 cp
features: Plain bed
Chairs
Tables
Other furnishings
